origin_lemma.etymology: 9424 bhástrā f. 'leathern bag' ŚBr., 'bellows' Kāv., bhastrikā- f. 'little bag' Daś. [Despite EWA ii 489, not from a √bhas 'blow' (existence of which is very doubtful). — Basic meaning is 'skin bag' (cf. bakura- 'bellows' ~ bākurá-dŕ̥ti- 'goat's skin'), der. from bastá- m. 'goat' RV. (cf. bastājina- n. 'goat's skin' MaitrS. = bāstaṁ carma Mn.); with bh- (and unexpl. -st-) in Pa. bhasta- m. 'goat', bhastacamma- n. 'goat's skin'. Phonet. Pa. and all NIA. (except S. with a) may be < *bhāsta-, cf. bāsta- above (J. C. W.)]

Ralph Lilley Turner\.
*A comparative dictionary of the Indo\-Aryan languages*\.
Oxford University Press, 1962–1966\.
